📄 Complete Details & Notification

The Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) published the final answer key and provisional result for the KSRP/KSISF/IRB Police Constable competitive examination on 25 September 2026. This covers candidates from both the Residual Parent Cadre (RPC, state-wide KSRP) and the Kalyana Karnataka local cadre (KSRP, KSISF, and IRB posts under Article 371(J)). The written exam for this recruitment was held on 20 September 2026. This article explains exactly what KEA has announced, the objection window still open, and how to check your provisional result.

Direct Link to Download KSRP Police Constable Result 2026 Here

KSRP Police Constable Result 2026 - Quick Overview

Particulars Details
Conducting Authority Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA)
Recruiting Department Karnataka State Police Department
Posts Covered Special Reserve Police Constable (KSRP) - Residual Parent Cadre; KSRP, Police Constable (KSISF), and Special Reserve Police Constable (IRB) - Kalyana Karnataka local cadre

Event Date
Written competitive examination 20 September 2026

Objection window for provisional answer key Until 10:30 AM, 23 September 2026
Final (revised) answer key published 25 September 2026
Provisional result published 25 September 2026
Objection window for provisional result Until 5:30 PM, 27 September 2026

How to Check Your KSRP Police Constable Provisional Result

  1. Go to the official KEA website: cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea.
  2. Look for the notice regarding the KSRP/KSISF/IRB Police Constable provisional result and final answer key, dated 25 September 2026.
  3. Open the relevant link for your cadre - Residual Parent Cadre (RPC) or Kalyana Karnataka (KK) - as provided on the site.
  4. Enter the login details requested (typically your application/roll number and date of birth).
  5. View your marks in the provisional result.
  6. Download or save a copy for your records.

Also Read: UPSSSC Assistant Store Keeper Final Result 2026

How to Submit an Objection to the Provisional Result

  • Objections must be submitted online through cetonline.karnataka.gov.in/kea.
  • Deadline: 5:30 PM, 27 September 2026.
  • Supporting documents must be attached - objections without documents will not be considered.
  • Objections relating to the final answer key itself will not be accepted at this stage, since that window has already closed.

How to Check Your Name in the CSIR-NEIST Result List

SSSB Punjab JSS Result 2026: Overall Statistics

Based on the 132 roll numbers listed in the official result document:

  • Total candidates in the list: 132
  • Candidates marked Absent in both Punjabi and English papers: 66
  • Candidates who appeared but were marked N.Q. (Not Qualified) in both papers: 60
  • Candidates with a recorded mistake score in at least one paper (while still N.Q. in the other): 6

Based strictly on the entries in the official PDF, none of the 132 listed candidates show a qualifying/numeric mistake score in both the Punjabi and English papers simultaneously - every candidate has either "Absent" or "N.Q." in at least one of the two language columns. This is a factual observation from the published data and not an interpretation of SSSB Punjab's selection criteria, which is not stated in the document.

Category-Wise Breakdown

  • B.C (Backward Class) category candidates: 91

Selection Process 

The final selection is based on the total marks obtained in the written examination and interview combined (900 marks). Where more than one candidate obtains equal total marks, the Commission applies the following tie-break rules, in order:

  3. If the written examination marks are also equal, the candidate with a higher age is given preference.

What After RBI Assistant Mains Result 2026?

Candidates shortlisted in the Mains Result must now appear for the Language Proficiency Test (LPT), the final stage of the RBI Assistant selection process. The LPT tests a candidate's ability to read, write, speak, and understand the official/local language of the RBI office for which they applied. Candidates who studied the relevant local language up to the 10th or 12th standard are generally exempted; others must appear for and clear the LPT to remain in contention for final selection. The LPT is qualifying in nature no marks from it are added to the final merit list, but clearing it is mandatory. RBI is yet to announce the exact LPT schedule, venue, and reporting-time details for this cycle; candidates should watch the official portal for this notification.

RBI Assistant Selection Process 2026

  • Preliminary Examination: Qualifying stage only. Prelims marks are not counted towards the final merit list.
  • Main Examination: The Mains score is what decides a candidate's final rank and selection.
  • Language Proficiency Test (LPT): Qualifying stage. Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the local/regional language of the RBI office applied for. There is no interview stage in this recruitment.

  • Candidates who fail to submit the required originals will not be allowed to join.
  • The Bank states it has taken adequate care in compiling the list and reserves the right to rectify any inadvertent errors.

The SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 has been released by the State Bank of India on 1st September 2026, following the declaration of the SBI PO Prelims Result on 28th August 2026. Candidates who appeared in the Probationary Officer Preliminary Examination held on 1st and 2nd August 2026 can now check their total and section-wise marks online. This page covers the direct download link, step-by-step download process, details shown on the scorecard, qualifying status, cut-off information, and the next steps before the SBI PO Mains Exam 2026.

Direct Link to Check SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

Quick Overview - SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

The SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 is a mark-sheet issued to every candidate who appeared in the Preliminary Examination, whether or not they qualified for the Mains stage. It shows the marks obtained in each section along with the total score and qualifying status. Prelims marks are used only for shortlisting candidates for the Mains exam and are not added to the final merit list.

  • SBI PO Prelims Exam: 1 and 2 August 2026

  • SBI PO Mains Exam: 12 September 2026

SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 Direct Link

The direct link to check the SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 is active on the official SBI recruitment portal. Candidates should use only the official link below rather than unofficial third-party websites to avoid entering their details on unsafe pages.

SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026 - Official Download Link

Details Required to Check SBI PO Score Card 2026

Candidates need the following details ready before logging in to check their score card. Source reports on the exact second login field are inconsistent — some describe it as the account password, others as the date of birth. Keep both on hand to avoid a failed login attempt.

  • Registration Number or Roll Number (mandatory)
  • Password or Date of Birth, depending on the login screen displayed (see discrepancy note below)
  • Captcha / text verification code

How to Download SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

  1. Visit the official SBI website at sbi.co.in and go to the Careers section.
  2. Click on "Current Openings" and find the Probationary Officer recruitment link (CRPD/PO/2026-27/09).
  3. Click on the "SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026" or "Marks Secured by the Candidates in Preliminary Examination" link.
  4. Enter your Registration Number or Roll Number.
  5. Enter your Password or Date of Birth, as prompted on screen.
  6. Enter the captcha/verification code and click Submit.
  7. Your SBI PO Prelims Score Card will appear on the screen.
  8. Check all details carefully and download or take a printout for future reference.

Details Mentioned in SBI PO Prelims Score Card 2026

The SBI PO Score Card 2026 displays the following details. Candidates are advised to verify every field carefully and report any discrepancy to SBI through the official channel.

Field Description
Candidate Name As per application form
Roll Number / Registration Number Unique candidate identifier
Date of Birth As per application form
Category General/EWS/OBC/SC/ST/PwBD as applicable
Post Applied For Probationary Officer
Exam Date 1 or 2 August 2026 (as applicable to the candidate's shift)
Section-Wise Marks Marks obtained in each Prelims section
Total Marks / Aggregate Score Overall score out of 100
Qualifying Status Qualified / Not Qualified for Mains

Important Instructions for SBI PO Score Card 2026

  • Use only the official SBI website or Careers portal to check and download your score card; avoid third-party links.
  • Keep your Registration Number/Roll Number, Date of Birth, and password handy before attempting to log in.
  • Cross-check the domain name in your browser address bar before entering personal details.
  • Download and save a copy of the score card for future reference, as it may be required at later stages of recruitment.
  • In case of login errors, this can occur due to incorrect details, heavy website traffic, or a temporary technical issue — wait and retry rather than repeatedly submitting incorrect information.
  • Report any factual error on your score card to SBI through the official grievance/contact channel rather than assuming it will self-correct.

SBI PO Mains Exam 2026: Next Step

Candidates shortlisted through the SBI PO Prelims Result 2026 will appear for the SBI PO Mains Examination scheduled on 12th September 2026. The Mains exam includes both an objective test and a descriptive paper, with negative marking of 0.25 marks per wrong answer applicable to the objective section only. The SBI PO Mains Admit Card release date is Not Available Officially at the time of this update. Shortlisted candidates are advised to use their Prelims score card to identify weaker sections and focus preparation accordingly on reasoning, data analysis, English language, general/economy/banking awareness, and descriptive writing.

How to Download RBI Assistant Prelims Score Card 2026

  1. Visit the official RBI recruitment portal at rbi.org.in and go to the "Opportunities@RBI" section, or use the direct score card login link on the official results page.
  2. Click on "Current Vacancies," then locate the RBI Assistant Recruitment 2026 (Panel Year 2025) link.
  3. Open the "Marksheet of Preliminary Examination" or "Score Card" link for the Assistant post.
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number in the first field.
  5. Enter your Password (this is generally your Date of Birth, in DD-MM-YY format).
  6. Type the Captcha code exactly as shown.
  7. Click the Submit button.
  8. Your score card will be displayed on the screen download and save it, or take a printout for future reference.

RBI Assistant Prelims Cut Off 2026

The category-wise and office-wise cut off marks have been released alongside the score card. The cut off table indicates the minimum qualifying marks for General, SC, ST, OBC, EWS, PwBD, and Ex-Servicemen categories, along with sectional cut off marks for each subject. Where no vacancy exists for a category at a particular office, the cut off may be shown as "-", and in some cases all qualified candidates are merit-listed rather than shortlisted against a fixed cut off.

Important Instructions

  • Verify every detail on your score card carefully, including your name, roll number, category, and marks.
  • RBI does not send score cards through email or SMS they must be downloaded manually from the official portal.
  • Compare your marks against the official category-wise cut off before assuming your qualifying status.
  • If any information on your score card appears incorrect, contact RBI through the official channels mentioned on the recruitment portal.
  • Keep a downloaded copy or printout of the score card for future reference, including for the Mains stage and beyond.
  • Start preparing for the Mains Examination immediately, focusing on sections where your sectional marks were relatively weaker.

Union Bank of India Apprentice Selection Process

As per the result notice, final selection depends on successful completion of the following activities after the provisional result:

  2. Language Proficiency Test (for applicable candidates).

The Bank has clearly stated that selection is provisional and subject to production of all relevant documentary evidence supporting eligibility at the time of reporting.

Documents Required for Union Bank of India Apprentice Document Verification

Selected candidates must carry the following documents at the time of reporting:

  • 10 photographs (as uploaded on the NATS Portal)
  • Address Proof (Permanent and Communication)
  • PAN Card / Proof of PAN allotment
  • Aadhaar Card
  • All original certificates supporting eligibility (10th/Matriculation, 12th onwards) — both Degree and Marksheet must be produced

Important Instructions for the IBPS PO Mains Exam

Candidates must follow these exam-day guidelines carefully:

  • Carry a printed copy of the IBPS PO Mains Admit Card along with an original valid photo ID proof.
  • Reach the exam centre at least 30 to 45 minutes before the reporting time mentioned on the call letter.
  • Carry 2 to 3 passport-size photographs identical to the one uploaded on the call letter.
  • Electronic devices, smartwatches, calculators, Bluetooth devices, and study materials are not allowed inside the exam hall.
  • Biometric verification will be conducted at the exam centre to maintain the integrity of the process.
  • Ensure the photograph and signature printed on the admit card are clear and legible.

If you notice any mistake or discrepancy on your IBPS PO Mains Admit Card, follow these steps:

  1. Verify your name spelling, date of birth, registration number, and category carefully.
  2. Check whether your photograph and signature are clearly visible.
  3. Confirm the centre name, shift timing, and full address are correct.
  4. Contact the IBPS helpdesk through the official support email or helpline number given on the portal.
  5. Keep your online application form and registration acknowledgement ready for faster resolution.
  6. Download the corrected admit card once the issue has been updated by IBPS.

IBPS PO Mains Exam Date and Pattern 2026

The IBPS PO Mains exam will be held on 4 October 2026. It is a Computer-Based Test that evaluates candidates on Reasoning & Computer Aptitude, General/Economy/Banking Awareness, English Language, and Data Analysis & Interpretation, along with a descriptive English Language Writing Test (Essay & Letter). Negative marking applies for wrong answers in the objective sections. Exact sectional timings, marks distribution, and negative-marking ratio are not available in the source material used for this article and should be checked on the admit card and the official notification.

  5. Download and print your admit card, and carefully note your allotted interview date, reporting time, and venue.

Interview / DV Venue

The reporting venue stated in the official interview schedule is the Punjab and Haryana High Court Extension-II, Sector 17, Chandigarh (Bridge Market). A separate secondary source additionally lists the Chandigarh Judicial Academy, Sector 43, Chandigarh, as a venue for some candidates this second venue is not confirmed in the primary source used for this article, so candidates should rely on the venue printed on their own individual admit card rather than either listing here.

Documents Required for Interview / Document Verification

The exact document checklist for each candidate is printed on their individual e-admit card. In general, candidates appearing for this interview-cum-document verification should carry:

  • Downloaded e-admit card / interview call letter (original)
  • Valid original photo ID proof
  • Original educational and experience/diploma certificates claimed in the application, with self-attested photocopies
  • Category certificate (SC/ST/BC), if applicable, issued by the appropriate state authority
  • Age proof document
  • Passport-size photographs, as specified on the admit card

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • Carry your original e-admit card along with valid original photo ID to the interview venue entry without these may be refused.
  • Reach the venue well before the reporting time printed on your admit card.
  • Carry originals plus self-attested photocopies of all documents claimed in your application.
  • Do not rely on unofficial channels or agents for updates; verify all information only from highcourtchd.gov.in.
  • Since reported interview end-dates and venue details vary across secondary sources, always confirm your specific date, time, and venue from your own admit card rather than any third-party article, including this one.

Eligibility Criteria

Candidates must meet the educational qualification, age limit, and nationality conditions set by the Central Bank of India to be eligible for the Apprentice post.

Educational Qualification

  • Candidates should have completed graduation on or after 1 January 2022 (some sources indicate the cut-off as 1 January 2021; candidates should verify the exact date on the official notification).
  • Candidates with one year or more of work or training experience after graduation are not eligible, since this scheme is meant for fresh graduates.
  • Candidates who have already completed apprenticeship training, or are currently undergoing apprenticeship training elsewhere, are not eligible.
  • Basic computer knowledge is required.
  • Candidates must be proficient in the local language of the state they are applying for.

Age Limit

Candidates must be between 20 and 28 years of age as on 31 May 2026, meaning they should be born between 31 May 1998 and 31 May 2006 (both dates inclusive).

Final selection also depends on document verification and meeting the required medical fitness standards set by the bank.

RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026 - Phase 1 Out, Mains Hall Ticket Expected in July

The Reserve Bank of India has officially released the RBI Grade B Phase 1 Admit Card 2026 on its official portal at rbi.org.in. Candidates who applied for the Grade B Officer (General Cadre) post can download their Phase 1 call letter using their Registration Number and Date of Birth. The Phase 1 exam for the General post was conducted on 13th June 2026, while the Phase 2 Mains exam is scheduled for 25th July 2026 and the Mains admit card is now the next major release that candidates are eagerly waiting for.

This article covers everything you need to know about the RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026 from the Phase 1 call letter download process to the expected Mains hall ticket release date, exam shift timings, documents to carry, and exam pattern details.

RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026 - Quick Overview

This section gives a snapshot of all key details related to the RBI Grade B 2026 exam and admit card in one place, so candidates can quickly check the current status and upcoming dates.

Particulars Details
Conducting Authority Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
Post Name Officer Grade B - General / DEPR / DSIM
Total Vacancies 60
Phase 1 Exam Date (General) 13th June 2026
Phase 1 Exam Date (DEPR/DSIM) 14th June 2026
Phase 1 Admit Card Release Date 5th June 2026
Phase 1 Admit Card Status Released
Phase 2 (Mains) Exam Date - General 25th July 2026
Phase 2 (Mains) Exam Date - DEPR/DSIM 26th July 2026
Phase 2 Admit Card Status Expected in July 2026
Exam Mode Online (CBT)
Selection Process Phase 1 → Phase 2 → Interview
Official Website rbi.org.in

RBI Grade B Phase 1 Admit Card 2026 - Released

The RBI Grade B Phase 1 call letter was released on 5th June 2026, ahead of the Phase 1 examination held on 13th June 2026. The call letter was made available through the official RBI recruitment portal and candidates were required to log in with their registration credentials to access it. This section also applies to candidates of DEPR and DSIM posts, whose Phase 1 exam was scheduled for 14th June 2026.

The Phase 1 exam is qualifying in nature only scores from this stage are used solely to shortlist candidates for Phase 2 (Mains). Marks from Phase 1 do not contribute to the final merit list.

RBI Grade B Mains Admit Card 2026 - Expected in July

With Phase 1 completed, all attention now turns to the RBI Grade B Phase 2 Mains Admit Card 2026, which is expected to be released in July 2026, ahead of the Mains exam scheduled on 25th July 2026 for General posts and 26th July 2026 for DEPR/DSIM posts. RBI typically releases the Mains hall ticket approximately 7 to 10 days before the exam date, so candidates should watch the official website closely during the second week of July.

The Mains exam is a comprehensive paper that tests a candidate's knowledge of Economic and Social Issues, Finance and Management, and English Writing Skills. Unlike Phase 1, Phase 2 marks are directly counted in the final selection.

 

How to Download RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026

Downloading the RBI Grade B call letter is a straightforward process. The same steps apply for both Phase 1 (already released) and Phase 2 (upcoming). Follow the steps below to access your hall ticket from the official website.

Step 1: Visit the official RBI recruitment portal at https://opportunities.rbi.org.in/

Step 2: Look for the admit card link under the "Call Letter" section select the link for the relevant phase (Phase 1 or Phase 2).

Step 3: A login page will appear on your screen.

Step 4: Enter your Registration Number and Date of Birth / Password in the respective fields.

Step 5: Click on the Submit button. Your RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026 will be displayed on the screen.

Step 6: Carefully verify all the details printed on the call letter name, roll number, exam centre, and shift timing.

Step 7: Download and take at least 2 printouts to carry on exam day.

Step 8: Read all exam day instructions mentioned on the call letter before the examination.

Details to Verify on Your RBI Grade B Call Letter

After downloading the admit card, candidates must cross-check the following details to ensure everything is accurate. If any discrepancy is found, it must be reported to RBI's recruitment authorities immediately.

The call letter will contain the following information:

Candidate's Name, Roll Number and Registration Number, Photograph and Signature, Date of Birth, Category (UR/OBC/SC/ST/EWS/PwBD), Post Applied For, Exam Date and Shift Timing, Reporting Time and Gate Closing Time, Exam Centre Name, Address, and Code, and Important Exam Day Instructions.

Documents to Carry to the RBI Grade B Exam Centre

Carrying the right documents to the examination centre is mandatory. Entry will not be granted if the candidate fails to produce valid identity proof along with the printed admit card.

Every candidate must bring the following on exam day:

Printed copy of the RBI Grade B Admit Card 2026, 2 recent passport-size photographs, one valid original Photo ID proof such as Aadhaar Card, PAN Card, Passport, Voter ID, or Driving Licence, and a photocopy of the same Photo ID.

PwBD candidates should additionally refer to the Instructions for PwBD Candidates using Scribe and/or Compensatory Time document available on the official website.

RBI Grade B Phase 1 Shift Timing 2026

The Phase 1 exam for General posts was conducted on 13th June 2026 in a single shift. Candidates were required to arrive at the exam centre well before the gate closing time. The general shift schedule for the exam is outlined below.

Exam Phase Reporting Time Gate Closing Time Exam Time
Phase 1 1:00 PM 1:45 PM 2:00 PM - 4:00 PM

Note: Individual admit cards may contain slightly different timings based on centre and shift allocation. Always follow the timing printed on your specific call letter.

RBI Grade B Exam Pattern 2026

Understanding the exam pattern helps candidates prepare effectively for both phases of the selection process. The RBI Grade B selection consists of Phase 1 (Prelims), Phase 2 (Mains), and an Interview round.

Phase 1 Exam Pattern - Objective Type (Qualifying)

Phase 1 is a 2-hour online objective exam carrying 200 marks across 200 questions. Since it is only qualifying, candidates must clear it to advance to Mains, but these marks do not count toward the final score.

Section Questions Marks Duration
Reasoning Ability 60 60 45 Minutes
English Language 30 30 25 Minutes
Quantitative Aptitude 30 30 25 Minutes
General Knowledge (GA) 80 80 25 Minutes
Total 200 200 120 Minutes

Phase 2 (Mains) Exam Pattern - Objective + Descriptive

Phase 2 is the main scoring round with 300 marks spread across 3 papers. Both objective and descriptive components are tested. Marks from this stage directly determine the final merit list.

Paper Subject Question Type Marks Duration
Paper I Economic & Social Issues (ESI) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Paper II English (Writing Skills) Descriptive 100 90 Minutes
Paper III Finance & Management (FM) Objective + Descriptive 100 120 Minutes
Total     300 330 Minutes

RBI Grade B Exam Day Instructions 2026

RBI has issued specific instructions that every candidate must follow on exam day. Non-compliance may result in disqualification from the examination.

Candidates must reach the exam centre before the gate closing time without fail. Biometric verification including thumb impression and photograph capture will be conducted at the centre. Ensure your name on the admit card matches exactly with your photo ID. Wearing clothes with metal items, large buttons, or accessories that could trigger security checks should be avoided. Electronic devices including mobile phones, smart watches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, and books are strictly prohibited inside the examination hall. The exam centre and date allotted on the call letter are final no requests for change of centre, date, or session will be entertained.

Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026 - Download Link

Bank of Baroda has released the Bank of Baroda (BOB) Apprentice Admit Card 2026 for candidates who applied for the 5,000 Apprentice vacancies. The call letter is available on the bank's official career portal, bankofbaroda.bank.in, and candidates can download it by logging in with their registration number and password or date of birth. The online examination is scheduled for June 21, 2026 (Sunday), and the hall ticket is mandatory for entry into the exam centre. Below is everything you need to know the direct download steps, key dates, exam pattern, and what to carry on exam day.

Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026: Key Highlights

This section gives a quick snapshot of the most important facts about the BOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026 organisation, posts, dates, and exam mode so you can verify the essentials at a glance before going into the details.

Particulars Details
Organisation Bank of Baroda (BOB)
Post Name Apprentice
Total Vacancies 5,000
Application Start Date 19 May 2026
Application Last Date 8 June 2026
Admit Card Release Date 19 June 2026
Online Exam Date 21 June 2026 (Sunday)
Mode of Exam Online (Computer-Based Test)
Exam Duration 60 minutes
Total Questions/Marks 100 questions / 100 marks
Negative Marking None
Stipend (if selected) ₹15,000 per month during a 1-year apprenticeship
Official Website bankofbaroda.bank.in

Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026 Download Link

Candidates who successfully applied for the BOB Apprentice recruitment between 19 May and 8 June 2026 can now access their admit card online. The hall ticket has been hosted on the official Bank of Baroda careers page, and candidates need their login credentials handy before they try to download it.

  • Official admit card portal: bankofbaroda.bank.in
  • Click Here: Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • Candidates are advised to download and save the admit card well before exam day to avoid last-minute server load or technical glitches.

Bank of Baroda Apprentice Exam Date 2026

This section answers the most commonly searched question when is the BOB Apprentice exam happening. The online test is a single-day, single-shift computer-based exam.

The Bank of Baroda Apprentice Online Examination 2026 is scheduled for June 21, 2026 (Sunday). Candidates should plan their travel to the allotted exam centre in advance and check their reporting time as mentioned on the admit card to avoid last-minute stress.

Credentials Required to Download BOB Apprentice Admit Card

Before logging in to the admit card portal, keep the following details ready. This information is typically the same combination used during registration.

  • Registration Number / Roll Number
  • Password or Date of Birth (as set/used during application)
  • If you have forgotten your password, use the "Forgot Password" option on the login page to retrieve or reset your credentials.

How to Download Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026

This step-by-step guide explains the exact process to access and download your hall ticket from the official website, so you can complete it without confusion.

  1. Visit the official Bank of Baroda website: bankofbaroda.bank.in.
  2. Navigate to the "Careers" or "Current Opportunities" section on the homepage.
  3. Click on the link that reads "Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card 2026."
  4. Enter your Registration Number/Roll Number and Password/Date of Birth in the login window.
  5. Click Submit to view your admit card on the screen.
  6. Check all the details carefully and download the admit card.
  7. Take a clear, color printout for use on exam day.

Details Mentioned on the Bank of Baroda Apprentice Admit Card

Once downloaded, candidates should cross-check every detail printed on the hall ticket immediately, since any discrepancy needs to be flagged to the bank well before the exam date.

The admit card typically includes:

  • Candidate's name, photograph, and signature
  • Registration number and roll number
  • Exam date, reporting time, and exam shift timing
  • Complete exam centre name and address
  • Important exam-day instructions and guidelines issued by the bank

Bank of Baroda Apprentice Exam Pattern 2026

This section explains how the BOB Apprentice online exam is structured, so candidates know exactly what to expect in terms of sections, marks, and timing.

The BOB Apprentice exam is an online objective-type test consisting of 100 questions for 100 marks, to be completed in 60 minutes. The paper is divided into four sections of equal weightage, with no sectional time limit unless specified otherwise in the official notification.

Section Number of Questions Marks
General / Financial Awareness 25 25
Quantitative & Reasoning Aptitude 25 25
Computer Knowledge 25 25
General English 25 25
Total 100 100

Key points about the exam pattern:

  • Each correct answer carries 1 mark.
  • There is no negative marking for wrong answers.
  • No marks are awarded for unattempted questions.
  • The question paper is available in English and Hindi, except for the General English section.

What to Carry on Exam Day

Carrying the right documents is essential, as candidates without a valid admit card or ID proof may be denied entry to the exam centre. This checklist covers what you must bring.

  • A clear, printed copy of the BOB Apprentice Admit Card 2026
  • A valid original photo ID proof (such as Aadhaar Card or PAN Card) the same ID used during the application process
  • A recent passport-size photograph
  • Arrive at the exam centre well before the reporting time mentioned on the admit card

What Happens After the Exam?

This section outlines the next stages of the selection process so candidates know what to expect once the online exam is over.

The Bank of Baroda Apprentice selection process does not end with the written exam. Candidates who qualify in the online test move to the following stages:

  1. Document Verification - Shortlisted candidates must produce original documents for eligibility verification.
  2. Language Proficiency Test - Candidates must demonstrate proficiency in the official local language of the state they applied for.
  3. Medical Examination - A final medical fitness check is conducted before confirmation of selection.

Selected apprentices will be engaged for a one-year apprenticeship period and will receive a stipend of ₹15,000 per month during this engagement.

Bank of Baroda (BoB), one of India's largest public sector banks, has released the Bank of Baroda Recruitment 2026 notification (Advt No. BOB/HRM/REC/ADVT/2026/17) for the regular-basis recruitment of Wealth Executive and Credit Analyst – C&IC (Corporate & Institutional Credit) posts. A total of 1,100 vacancies are on offer - 1,000 posts for Wealth Executive (JMG/S-I) under the Wealth Management Services department and 100 posts for Credit Analyst-C&IC (MMG/S-II) under the Corporate & Institutional Credit department. Online registration for Bank of Baroda Wealth Executive and Credit Analyst Recruitment 2026 starts on 04.09.2026 and closes on 01.10.2026. Eligible candidates can apply online through the bank's official website.

In short: Bank of Baroda is recruiting for Wealth Executive and Credit Analyst-C&IC posts, with 1,100 total vacancies (1,000 + 100). Graduates with the relevant certification/professional qualification and requisite experience, who are willing to serve anywhere in India, can apply. Applications open 04.09.2026 and close 01.10.2026, applications are accepted only in online mode, and selected candidates may be posted to any branch or office of the Bank across India.

Bank of Baroda has released the official notification PDF for Wealth Executive and Credit Analyst-C&IC Recruitment 2026 on its careers page. Candidates are advised to read the full notification carefully before applying.

Bank of Baroda Vacancy 2026 – Post Details

Bank of Baroda has announced 1,100 vacancies across two posts. The bank reserves the right to modify the number of vacancies depending on its requirement.

Bank of Baroda Wealth Executive & Credit Analyst Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility for both posts is assessed as on the cut-off date, 01.09.2026. Candidates must fulfil the mandatory qualification, experience, and age criteria specified below for the post they are applying for.

Educational Qualification

Post Qualification Post-Qualification Experience
Wealth Executive Graduation in any discipline AND any one valid certification among: IC 38 (Insurance Institute of India), NISM Series V A (Mutual Fund Distributors), NISM Series XXI-A (PMS Distributors), or NISM Series V-D (Mutual Fund – Specialised Investment Fund Distributors). Preferred: 2-year full-time PG degree/diploma in Management or MBA (Finance/Marketing/Banking). Minimum 2 years of experience in sales of wealth products with leading public/private/foreign banks, broking, securities firms, asset management companies, or wealth management companies in India.
Credit Analyst – C&IC Graduation in any discipline AND Chartered Accountant. Mandatory: minimum 1 year of banking experience in a Scheduled Commercial Bank. Preferred: experience in Corporate Credit.

Note: Post-qualification experience of less than six months in any organisation as on 01.09.2026 will not be considered for eligibility, except when it is part of current employment. Experience in clerical cadre is not considered for determining eligibility. Educational qualifications must be from a college/institution/university recognised by the Government of India/Government bodies/AICTE.

Bank of Baroda Wealth Executive & Credit Analyst Salary 2026

Selected candidates will be placed in the following pay scales, as amended from time to time. Salary and other emoluments are governed by the industry-level bipartite settlement and Joint Note applicable to officers in the banking sector, along with bank-specific allowances and perquisites.

Grade / Scale Pay Scale

General, EWS & OBC Rs. 850/- + Payment Gateway Charges
SC, ST, PWBD, ESM (Ex-Servicemen) & Women Rs. 175/- + Payment Gateway Charges

Payment can be made using Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI. Transaction charges, if any, are borne by the candidate.

Bank of Baroda Selection Process 2026

The selection process may comprise Application Scrutiny, an Online Test, Psychometric Test, Group Discussion (GD) and/or Personal Interview (PI), or any other test deemed suitable by the Bank.

Online Test Structure (Tentative, if Conducted)

Section Name of Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration Version
1 English Language 20 20 20 Minutes English
2 Reasoning Ability & Quantitative Aptitude 20 20 20 Minutes Bilingual
3 General / Economic & Banking Awareness 20 20 20 Minutes Bilingual
4 Professional Knowledge related to the Position 60 60 60 Minutes Bilingual
Total   120 120 120 Minutes  
  • Sections 1, 2 and 3 are qualifying in nature; marks in these sections are not reckoned for the merit list.
  • There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer; no penalty for unattempted questions.
  • The minimum qualifying marks/percentage for Personal Interview (PI) is 60% for General & EWS category and 55% for other Reserved categories; the Bank reserves the right to change this at its discretion.
  • Candidates not clearing the PI will not be considered for final selection.
  • A Psychometric Test and/or PI assesses personality, communication, problem-solving, efficiency, and willingness to work anywhere in the country.
  • The Bank's shortlisting criteria are internal and confidential and are not shared with candidates.

Probation Period & Service Bond

  • Selected candidates will be on probation for a period of 12 months (1 year) of active service from the date of joining.
  • JMG/S-I officers: must serve a minimum of 3 years, or pay an amount equal to three months' gross salary (not exceeding Rs. 2 lakh) if they leave before completing 3 years.
  • MMG/S-II officers: must serve a minimum of 3 years, or pay an amount equal to three months' gross salary (not exceeding Rs. 3 lakh) if they leave before completing 3 years.

Documents Required

Candidates must produce the following documents in original with self-attested photocopies at the time of interview/any subsequent stage:

  • Printout of the valid GD/Interview Call Letter
  • Valid system-generated printout of the online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate or SSLC/Std. X Certificate with DOB)
  • Photo Identity Proof (PAN Card/Passport/Driving License/Voter's Card/Aadhaar with photograph, etc. - Ration Card is NOT accepted)
  • Individual semester/year-wise mark sheets and certificates for educational qualifications, including the final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste Certificate (for SC/ST/OBC/EWS candidates) in the prescribed Government of India format
  • Disability Certificate in the prescribed format (for PwBD candidates)
  • Service/Discharge Book, pension payment order, and rank proof (for Ex-Servicemen)
  • No Objection Certificate (for candidates serving in Government/Quasi-Government offices or PSUs)
  • Certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India (for specified categories under nationality clause)
  • Relevant documents supporting declared work experience (appointment letter, salary slip, relieving letter, experience certificate)

How to Apply for Bank of Baroda Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official Bank of Baroda website: www.bankofbaroda.bank.in/Career.htm
  2. Navigate to Career section/web page > Current Opportunities and register online in the appropriate application format.
  3. Fill in the online application with accurate personal, educational, and category details. No change is permitted after clicking Submit.
  4. Upload the required documents: Resume, DOB proof, educational certificates, work experience certificates, caste/category certificate, and PwBD certificate (as applicable) - each in PDF format, page size A4, file size not exceeding 500 KB.
  5. Upload scanned photograph (200x230 pixels, 20–50 KB) and signature (140x60 pixels, 10–20 KB) as per the specifications in the notification.
  6. Upload left thumb impression image and hand-written declaration image as specified.
  7. Pay the application fee/intimation charges online using Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI.
  8. On successful payment, print and retain the system-generated e-receipt and application form for future reference.

The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) has released the notification for the Common Recruitment Process for Regional Rural Banks, 15th cycle (CRP RRBs-XV), inviting online applications for Group "A" Officer (Scale-I, II & III) and Group "B" Office Assistant (Multipurpose) posts across 28 Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) in India. IBPS RRB Recruitment 2026 online registration opens on 1 September 2026 and closes on 27 September 2026.

Quick answer: IBPS is recruiting for Officer Scale-I, II (seven specialisations), III, and Office Assistant (Multipurpose) posts, with an indicative 13,706 vacancies spread across 28 RRBs covering nearly every state and union territory of India. Graduates in any discipline (with specific additional qualifications for certain Officer Scale-II specialist roles) between 18 and 40 years of age (depending on the post) can apply online only, from 1 September 2026 to 27 September 2026, at the official IBPS website, www.ibps.in.

IBPS RRB Eligibility Criteria & Qualification

Nationality: a candidate must be a citizen of India, or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee who arrived before 1 January 1962 intending to settle permanently in India, or a person of Indian origin migrated from certain specified countries with an eligibility certificate from the Government of India.

Educational qualification (as on the last date of online registration, i.e. 21.09.2026) varies by post:

Post Essential Educational Qualification Post-Qualification Experience
Office Assistant (Multipurpose) Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university or equivalent; proficiency in the local language prescribed by the participating RRB; working knowledge of computers is desirable Not required
Officer Scale-I (Assistant Manager) Bachelor's degree in any discipline; preference to candidates with a degree in Agriculture, Horticulture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry, Veterinary Science, Agricultural Engineering, Pisciculture, Agricultural Marketing and Cooperation, IT, Management, Law, Economics or Accountancy; local language proficiency required Not required
Officer Scale-II - General Banking Officer Bachelor's degree in any discipline with minimum 50% aggregate marks; preference to specified subject backgrounds 2 years as an officer in a bank or financial institution
Officer Scale-II - Information Technology Officer Bachelor's degree in Electronics/Communication/Computer Science/IT or equivalent, minimum 50% aggregate marks 1 year in the relevant field
Officer Scale-II - Chartered Accountant Certified Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India 1 year as a Chartered Accountant
Officer Scale-II - Law Officer Degree in Law from a recognised university, minimum 50% aggregate marks 2 years as an advocate, or as a Law Officer in a bank/financial institution
Officer Scale-II - Treasury Manager Chartered Accountant, or MBA in Finance from a recognised university/institution 1 year in the relevant field
Officer Scale-II - Marketing Officer MBA in Marketing from a recognised university 1 year in the relevant field
Officer Scale-II - Agricultural Officer Bachelor's degree in Agriculture/Horticulture/Dairy/Animal Husbandry/Forestry/Veterinary Science/Agricultural Engineering/Pisciculture, minimum 50% aggregate marks 2 years in the relevant field

Candidates awarded CGPA/OGPA must convert it to a percentage as per their university's own conversion criteria, and the result for the qualifying degree must have been declared on or before 27.09.2026.

Post Age Limit

Age relaxation is available as follows: 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC (non-creamy layer), 10 years for Persons with Benchmark Disability (PwBD), and additional relaxation for Ex-Servicemen and (for Office Assistant only) widows, divorced women, and women legally separated from their husbands who have not remarried. Relaxation for SC/ST/OBC is cumulative with only one other applicable category.

IBPS RRB Salary & Exam Pattern

Salary: Not specified in the notification.

Exam pattern: The online examination structure differs by post and stage.

Post Stage Sections Total Marks Duration
Office Assistant / Officer Scale-I Preliminary Reasoning, Numerical Ability/Quantitative Aptitude 80 45 minutes
Office Assistant / Officer Scale-I Main Reasoning, Computer Knowledge, General Awareness, English/Hindi Language, Numerical Ability/Quantitative Aptitude 200 120 minutes
Officer Scale-III (Single-level exam) Single Reasoning, Computer Knowledge, Financial Awareness, English/Hindi Language, Quantitative Aptitude & Data Interpretation 200 120 minutes

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer in the objective tests; unattempted questions are not penalised. Officer Scale-II candidates sit for a single-level examination (structure not itemised separately in the notification excerpt reviewed here beyond the general pattern above).

Also read: IBPS RRB Clerk Exam Pattern and Syllabus 2026: Download PDF Here

IBPS RRB Selection Process

  • Office Assistant (Multipurpose): Preliminary Exam → Main Exam → Provisional Allotment (based on Main Exam marks and actual vacancies reported by the RRB).
  • Officer Scale-I: Preliminary Exam → Main Exam → Common Interview → Provisional Allotment.
  • Officer Scale-II & III: Single-level online exam → Common Interview → Provisional Allotment.
  • Interview is out of 100 marks; minimum qualifying marks are 40% (35% for SC/ST/OBC/PwBD candidates).
  • The relative weightage for Officer posts is 80% online exam and 20% interview.
  • Interviews for Officer posts are coordinated by the Nodal Regional Rural Bank with the assistance of NABARD and IBPS.

How to Apply for IBPS RRB Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official IBPS website, www.ibps.in, and open the "CRP for RRBs" link on the home page.
  2. Click "CLICK HERE TO APPLY ONLINE FOR CRP-RRBs-OFFICERS (Scale-I, II and III)" or "CLICK HERE TO APPLY ONLINE FOR CRP-RRBs-OFFICE ASSISTANTS (Multipurpose)", as applicable.
  3. Click "CLICK HERE FOR NEW REGISTRATION" and enter basic details to generate a provisional registration number and password (also sent by SMS/email).
  4. Log back in using the provisional registration number and password to complete the rest of the form.
  5. Upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression, a handwritten declaration, and your Class 10 (SSC/SSLC) certificate, plus any category/disability certificates applicable to you, as per the scanning specifications in Annexure-III.
  6. Pay the application fee/intimation charges online.
  7. Candidates applying for both Office Assistant and an Officer post, or reconsidering their choice of Officer scale, must register and pay separately for each post.
  8. Take a printout of the final submitted application form for future reference.

Documents Required

  • Printout of the valid interview call letter (for Officer posts)

  • Proof of date of birth (birth certificate or Class 10/SSLC certificate showing DOB)

  • Experience certificate(s), where the post requires post-qualification experience
  • Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC-NCL, in the prescribed Government of India format), where applicable
  • Income and Asset Certificate for EWS candidates, where applicable
  • Disability certificate/UDID card, where applicable
  • Ex-servicemen documents (discharge certificate/pension payment order, or the relevant proforma), where applicable

Specialist Grade II (Cardiology) 48 years (OBC); +10 years further relaxable for PwBD

General Age Relaxation (All Posts)

  • The listed age limit is normal for EWS/UR; relaxed by 5 years for SC/ST, 3 years for OBC, and 10 years for PwBD, in respect of vacancies reserved for them
  • Ex-Servicemen/Commissioned Officers: 5 years' relaxation (subject to at least 6 months' continuous service after attestation as on the closing date)
  • Central/UT Government servants: up to 5 years (10 years for SC/ST, 8 years for OBC posts reserved for them), subject to 3 years' continuous service in an allied cadre
  • PwBD candidates: 10 years' relaxation (so SC/ST-PwBD get up to 15 years total, OBC-PwBD up to 13 years total), subject to maximum age on closing date not exceeding 56 years; disability must be 40% or more

Post Pay Level (7th CPC) Group/Nature

Assistant Legislative Counsel Level-11 Group "A" Gazetted, Grade-IV Indian Legal Service; permanent; probation 2 years
Law Officer Level-07 General Central Service Group "B" Gazetted, Non-Ministerial; permanent; probation 2 years + mandatory 2-week induction training
Specialist Grade II (Cardiology) Level-11 plus NPA Group "A" Gazetted, Non-Ministerial; permanent; probation 1 year; private practice prohibited (NPA given instead)

UPSC Advt 12/2026 Selection Process

Selection is by interview, or by a Recruitment Test (RT)/Combined Recruitment Test (CRT) followed by interview, depending on the number of applications received for a post. There is no fixed CBT syllabus published for these posts in the advertisement.

  • Where applications are numerous, UPSC may apply shortlisting criteria: higher desirable qualifications, higher-than-minimum educational qualification, higher-than-minimum relevant experience, experience before/after acquiring essential qualification, experience not otherwise prescribed, or a Recruitment Test
  • Minimum level of suitability at interview (out of 100 marks): UR–50, OBC–45, SC/ST/PH–40
  • Where an RT precedes the interview, candidates must clear the minimum suitability level at both stages; the RT qualifying level is decided case-by-case by UPSC
  • Where an RT/CRT is held, it will ordinarily be conducted at: Ahmedabad, Bhopal, Chennai, Delhi, Dispur (Guwahati), Jaipur, Jammu, Kochi, Kolkata, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, Port Blair, Ranchi, and Visakhapatnam (Leh/Kargil/Srinagar/Delhi for Ladakh UT posts)
  • Candidature is provisional at every stage; mere fulfilment of minimum qualification/experience does not guarantee a call for interview
  • Where sufficient eligible PwBD candidates are not available for exclusively-reserved posts, the experience requirement (years, not nature) may be relaxed up to 50%

How to Apply for UPSC Advt 12/2026

  1. Visit upsconline.nic.in and create an account, if not already registered.
  2. Complete Universal Registration (generates a Universal Registration Number, or URN, common across all UPSC recruitments) and the Common Application Form (CAF).
  3. Fill the post/vacancy-specific fourth module for the post you are applying to; this generates a post-specific Application Number.
  4. Upload your photograph and capture a live photo as part of the CAF; sign three times on plain white paper in black ink and upload the signature.
  5. Upload supporting documents separately against each claim (date of birth, category, qualification, experience, etc.) as individual PDFs – do not upload pay slips, resumes, appointment/relieving letters, or unsigned experience certificates in this module.
  6. Pay the application fee of ₹25 online (Visa/Master/RuPay Card, UPI, or net banking), if applicable to your category.
  7. Review all entries carefully – no correction, alteration, or withdrawal is allowed after final submission.
  8. Submit before the closing date: 16 October 2026, 1800 hrs.
  9. Take a printout of the finally submitted application; you are not required to send this to UPSC by post, but must bring it (with original documents) if called for interview.

Application Fee

Category Fee
Unreserved / OBC / EWS (Male) ₹25
Women (all categories) / SC / ST / PwBD Exempted (Nil)
Important: Fee once paid is non-refundable and cannot be held in reserve for another exam/selection. Applications without the prescribed fee will be summarily rejected.

Documents Required

  • Matriculation/10th standard certificate or mark sheet showing date of birth
  • Degree/Diploma certificate as proof of educational qualification (or provisional certificate plus all mark sheets, if the final certificate is not yet issued)
  • Order/letter proving equivalence, if claiming a qualification as "equivalent" to the one prescribed
  • Experience certificate(s) in the prescribed proforma from the Head of Organisation/Department, clearly stating dates, pay, and nature of duties (part-time/daily-wage/guest-faculty experience is not counted)
  • Caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC) in the prescribed proforma from a competent authority; OBC candidates must also submit a non-creamy-layer declaration as on the closing date
  • Disability certificate in the prescribed proforma from a duly constituted Medical Board, for PwBD candidates
  • Certificate/document for age relaxation (Ex-servicemen, Central/UT Government employees, or special provisions), as applicable
  • Declaration by candidates already in regular Government service, confirming they have informed their Head of Office/Department of this application
  • Name-change documents (marriage/remarriage/divorce or other), if applicable
  • Certified translation (by a Gazetted Officer or notary) for any document not in Hindi or English

Important Conditions

  • Citizenship: Indian citizen, or a subject of Nepal/Bhutan, or a Tibetan refugee (pre-1962), or a person of Indian origin migrated from certain specified countries with an eligibility certificate from the Government of India
  • A candidate applying under UR cannot later claim a reserved category; requests to switch between reserved categories are not entertained; PwBD candidates cannot change their disability sub-category
  • Reserved-category candidates who fail to substantiate their claim by the prescribed stage will be considered against unreserved vacancies if they otherwise meet UR conditions
  • Mobile phones, smart watches, pen drives, cameras, Bluetooth devices, etc. are strictly banned in the examination/interview hall
  • Face authentication and identity verification are mandatory at the examination venue/interview hall
  • Scribe facility is available for specified PwBD categories (blindness, both-arms-affected locomotor disability, cerebral palsy automatically; others on production of a medical certificate)
  • Furnishing false particulars, impersonation, using unfair means, or misconduct can lead to disqualification, debarment (permanent or for a specified period) from UPSC exams and Central Government employment, and disciplinary/criminal action
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify a candidate
  • Outstation candidates called for interview at UPSC are reimbursed travel expenses restricted to Second/Sleeper Class train fare, paid via NEFT/bank transfer
  • Summoning for interview does not guarantee selection; UPSC may recommend higher initial pay for meritorious candidates
  • For the Law Officer post, GNCTD's own OBC reservation rules apply (a valid GNCTD-recognized OBC certificate, or one traceable to a GNCTD-issued family certificate for those settled in Delhi before 8 September 1993, is required)

Bank of India (BOI), a leading Public Sector Bank with its Head Office in Mumbai, has released a notification for the recruitment of Officers in various Specialist streams up to Scale IV. Under Project No. 2026-27/02 dated 01.08.2026, BOI is inviting applications for 205 vacancies across 48 distinct posts ranging from Officer (Scale I) to Chief Manager (Scale IV). Candidates with qualifications in Computer Science/IT, Law, Fire Engineering, and Civil Engineering can apply online between 10.09.2026 and 05.10.2026.

In brief: BOI is recruiting for IT and specialist officer roles spanning Full-Stack Engineering, Digital Platforms, Information Security, DevSecOps, Data Engineering, Database Administration, Law Officer, Fire Officer, Security Officer, and Civil Engineer, among others. Eligible Indian citizens (and other nationalities specified in the notice) meeting the post-specific qualification and experience criteria as on 01.08.2026 can apply online through the official BOI website. The application mode is online only, and postings will be anywhere in India.

HLL Lifecare Limited (HLL), India's leading manufacturer and marketer of contraceptive, healthcare and pharma products and a Mini Ratna Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, has invited online applications for 16 posts across departments such as Mental Health & Wellness, Lifepath, Allied Healthcare Services, Consumer Goods, Learning & Development, Legal, Pharma Retail, IT, HR, Secretarial, Civil, and Finance. Mineral Exploration and Consultancy Limited (MECL), a Mini-Ratna-I Central Public Sector Enterprise under the Ministry of Mines, Government of India, has invited online applications for 13 Executive Trainee posts in Electrical and Mechanical disciplines. Payment must be made online through Net-Banking or a QR code hosted on the MECL website under the Careers section. The fee, once paid, is non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other examination or selection.

MECL Executive Trainee Selection Process

The MECL Executive Trainee Recruitment 2026 selection process is based entirely on the UPSC ESE 2024 score, with no separate written examination or personal interview conducted by MECL:

  1. Applicant lists will be prepared in decreasing order of marks (out of 1200) scored in UPSC ESE 2024, category-wise, for the Mechanical/Electrical discipline.
  2. Eligible candidates will be shortlisted based on the UPSC ESE 2024 score and other eligibility criteria, as per MECL's extant Recruitment Rules.
  3. Shortlisted candidates will be called for a Document Verification round.
  4. If documents are found suitable and matching the advertisement criteria, offers of employment will be issued.

In case of a tie in total UPSC ESE 2024 score, seniority in age (as per Matriculation certificate) will be considered first, followed by a higher aggregate percentage in the essential engineering degree.

How to Apply for MECL Executive Trainee Recruitment 2026

Candidates can apply for the MECL Executive Trainee Recruitment 2026 by following these steps:

  1. Visit the official MECL website: www.mecl.co.in and go to the "Career" section.
  2. Register on the MECL Online Recruitment Portal with all mandatory details.
  3. Log in and click on "Apply for a Post" to fill the online application form.
  4. Enter personal details, educational qualification, UPSC ESE 2024 score, and category/community details accurately.
  5. Upload the required scanned documents in the specified format and file size.
  6. Pay the application fee (₹500 for General/OBC/EWS candidates, where applicable) online.
  7. Submit the application before the closing date of 14 August 2026.
  8. Take a printout of the system-generated application form for future reference.

Applications received through any mode other than the MECL Online Recruitment Portal will not be accepted and will be summarily rejected. Candidates are advised not to wait until the last date to apply.

MECL Executive Trainee Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Only Indian nationals are eligible to apply.
  • Selected candidates will undergo one year of training and may be posted at any MECL Project/Office/Establishment in India.
  • The appointee will be on probation for one year, extendable by up to one further year at the discretion of the Appointing Authority.
  • Executives/Executive Trainees must serve a minimum of 36 months after joining; a retention deduction of ₹5,000 per month will be made from salary, refundable (without interest) on completion of 36 months' service.
  • A service bond of ₹1.8 lakh must be executed to serve the company for a minimum of 36 months.
  • Appointment is subject to the candidate being declared medically fit by a Government Medical Officer/CMO of a Government Hospital, covering parameters such as vision, hearing, cardiovascular health, and more.
  • Category certificates must be valid as of the crucial date (01.08.2026); UPSC ESE 2024 category status does not automatically apply to MECL's process.
  • Candidates working in Central/State Government, PSUs, autonomous bodies, or nationalized banks must apply through proper channel or furnish a No Objection Certificate (NOC) at the time of document verification.
  • MECL reserves the right to increase, decrease, or not fill any of the advertised vacancies, or to cancel, restrict, enlarge, modify, or withdraw the recruitment process at any stage, without prior notice.
  • Corrigenda or amendments will be published only on the MECL website (www.mecl.co.in) under the Career section; no further press advertisement will be issued.
  • Candidates should not register more than once for the same post; if multiple applications are submitted, only the one with the higher Application Number will be considered.
  • For technical queries related to the MECL Recruitment Portal, candidates may email [email protected] with screenshots of the issue.

PMBI Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection for PMBI Recruitment 2026 follows a three-stage process:

  1. Initial Screening: The duly filled application form, along with copies of educational and experience documents, is checked and verified against the eligibility criteria for the post applied for.
  2. Written Examination: Screened eligible candidates are called for a written exam based on English language writing skills, subject knowledge related to the post, and general knowledge. No conveyance is paid for appearing in the written exam. Date, time, venue and syllabus are communicated to eligible candidates by email before the exam.
  3. Personal Interaction cum Interview: Candidates who qualify the written exam are called for a Personal Interaction cum Interview. Based on credentials and interview performance, the offer of appointment is issued to suitable candidates in order of merit. No TA/DA is paid for appearing in the interview.

Candidates must carry all original supporting documents (mark sheets, degree certificates, experience certificates, etc.) along with one set of photocopies at the time of the Personal Interaction cum Interview, for verification.

How to Apply for PMBI Recruitment 2026 (PMBI Recruitment 2026 Apply Online)

There is no online application portal mentioned in this PMBI notification. Applications must be submitted as hard copies only, by post or courier - applications sent by email or through any other mode will be rejected.

  1. Download the application form from the official website: https://www.pmbi.co.in/index.aspx
  2. Fill the application form completely, in the prescribed format only.
  3. Attach a recent passport-size photograph (selfies are not accepted).
  4. Attach self-attested copies of age proof (Matriculation Certificate/Aadhar Card/PAN Card/Passport), educational certificates, and experience certificates.
  5. Attach the original Demand Draft of Rs. 100 in favour of "Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India (PMBI)".
  6. Send the complete application by post/courier to: CEO, PMBI, B-500, Tower B, 5th Floor, World Trade Centre, Nauroji Nagar, New Delhi – 110029.
  7. Ensure the application reaches PMBI on or before 15 October 2026, till 5:00 PM.

Reasons Applications Will Be Rejected

  • Not submitted in the prescribed application format, or submitted through email/any other mode.
  • Missing age proof, educational certificates, experience certificates, or the Demand Draft.
  • Application or supporting documents submitted as photocopies/photos instead of originals with the form.
  • Application not clearly visible or not readable.
  • Application received after the last date and time.
  • Incomplete application, missing passport-size photo, or missing Rs. 100 Demand Draft.

PMBI Recruitment 2026: General Terms & Conditions

  • The appointment is purely contractual and does not entitle any candidate to claim regular/permanent employment in PMBI.
  • Selected candidates are liable to be transferred/posted anywhere in India at PMBI's discretion.
  • The initial contract is for 3 years, extendable based on performance; there is a 6-month observation period during the first year.
  • If an employee resigns or abandons service within the first year (including the observation period) or violates appointment terms, liquidated damages equal to 3 months' consolidated pay are payable.
  • During the 6-month observation period, the contract can be terminated by giving 7 days' notice if performance is unsatisfactory.
  • After the observation period, the contract can be terminated by giving 30 days' notice or 30 days' remuneration in lieu thereof.
  • The number of posts may be increased or decreased based on internal department requirements.
  • Candidates are advised to check their email regularly for updates; no TA/DA is paid for appearing in the interview.
  • For assistance, candidates may call PMBI on 011-49431800.

Key Eligibility Conditions

  • All full-time, part-time, and Open and Distance Learning (ODL) courses approved by AICTE and UGC are accepted, including Graduation and Post Graduation as specified.
  • Qualifications must be from a UGC-recognized university, AICTE-approved institution, or the concerned statutory council. Diploma qualifications must be recognized by the respective State Board of Technical Education; ITI/ NAC qualifications must be recognized by SCTVT/ NCTVT.
  • Post-qualification experience must be acquired after passing the respective course. Industrial/ Vocational/ Apprentice training under the Apprentices Act will not be counted as work experience.
  • Candidates working in Government/ Public Sector must have a minimum of one year's experience in the next lower pay scale or equivalent.

Selected candidates will be on probation for one year and will draw initial basic pay in the corresponding pay scale. In addition to Basic Pay, candidates are entitled to:

  • Perquisites @ 35% of basic pay
  • North-East allowance @ 10% of basic pay (if posted in the North-East region)
  • HRA
  • Conveyance Maintenance Expenses Reimbursement (CMER)
  • Medical Facility
  • Post Retirement Medical Scheme (PRMS)
  • Defined Contribution Pension Scheme (DCPS)

These are admissible as per Company rules in force and as amended from time to time.

BCPL Non Executive Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

  • Candidates meeting all eligibility criteria (as declared in the online Application Form) will be considered for further Selection Process.
  • Depending on the number of eligible applicants, the process may involve a single stage or multiple stages. If the number of applications is very high, BCPL may raise the minimum eligibility standards to shortlist candidates.
  • The Selection Process shall consist of Skill Test / Proficiency Test / Endurance Test / Written Test, and the exact process will be communicated in advance to shortlisted candidates.
  • The selection process indicated is tentative and may vary depending on administrative/ business requirements or Government of India directives.
  • Candidates must meet the prescribed medical fitness standards. Eye power criteria: for technical officers, total myopia should not exceed (-)4.00D and hypermetropia should not exceed (+)4.00D in each eye; for non-technical officers, myopia should not exceed (-)8.00D and hypermetropia should not exceed (+)6.00D (for candidates above 20 years).
  • No travelling expenses are payable to candidates called for the written test.

How to Apply for BCPL Non Executive Recruitment 2026

  1. Applications must be submitted online only through the official BCPL website: www.bcplonline.co.in. No other mode of application will be accepted.
  2. Candidates can apply for ONE post only. If a candidate submits more than one application, only the one submitted on the later date will be considered.
  3. Before applying, candidates should keep the following ready:
    • A valid e-mail ID (must remain active for at least one year; cannot be changed later)
    • A recent passport-size photograph and signature in digital form (.jpg/ .jpeg, under 50 KB)
    • Digital copies (.jpg/ .pdf, max 200 KB) of proof of age, SC/ ST/ EWS certificate, Benchmark Disability certificate (for PwBD), Ex-Servicemen certificate, mark sheets/ qualification certificates, and post-qualification experience certificates, as applicable.
  4. After submitting the application, candidates must download the system-generated Pay-in Slip and Registration Slip.
  5. Candidates are not required to submit a hard copy of the application form to BCPL.
  6. If shortlisted for the further Selection Process, candidates must carry the downloaded Application Form, original documents, and one self-attested photocopy set, including proof of date of birth, caste/ tribe certificate (if applicable), disability certificate (if applicable), ex-servicemen proof (if applicable), all qualification certificates from matriculation onward, and complete experience certificates as specified in the notification.
  7. Candidates employed in Central/ State Government, PSEs, or Autonomous Bodies must forward their application through the proper channel or produce a No Objection Certificate (NOC) at the time of the Selection Process.

Important General Instructions

  • The prescribed qualification/ experience represents the minimum standard only and does not automatically entitle a candidate to be called for further selection.
  • Details entered at the time of registration are final; requests to change mailing address, email ID, category, or post declared in the application will not be entertained.
  • Category (SC/ ST/ OBC-NCL/ EWS/ PwBD) once selected in the application cannot be changed later, and no benefit of another category will be given subsequently.
  • OBC candidates belonging to the Creamy Layer are not entitled to OBC concessions and must indicate their category as "General."
  • Furnishing false or incorrect information at any stage will lead to summary rejection of candidature, or termination of service if detected after appointment.
  • BCPL reserves the right to raise minimum eligibility standards, and to fill, not fill, cancel, restrict, enlarge, modify, or alter the recruitment/ selection process without prior notice.
  • Any dispute regarding this recruitment will be settled within the jurisdiction of Dibrugarh Court only, and the English version will prevail in case of any interpretation dispute with other language versions.
  • Any revision, clarification, addendum, or corrigendum to this advertisement will be published only on the "Careers" section of www.bcplonline.co.in.

UIIC AO Recruitment 2026 Overview

Particulars Details

UIIC AO Vacancy Details

UIIC has announced 225 provisional vacancies for Administrative Officer (Scale I) across two disciplines. The category-wise breakup, including the 4% horizontal reservation for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD), is given below. Note that these numbers are provisional and may vary as per the notification.

S. No. Post Name No. of Posts
1 Administrative Officer – Generalists 200 (UR-68, OBC-62, EWS-22, SC-30, ST-18; PwBD horizontal: VI-2, HI-2, OC-4, MD/ID-3)
2 Administrative Officer – Hindi Officers 25 (UR-11, OBC-7, EWS-2, SC-4, ST-1; PwBD horizontal: VI-1)

A candidate can apply for either Generalists or Hindi Officers, but not both. Multiple registrations or appearances will lead to cancellation of candidature. Candidates currently serving as Administrative Officers (Scale-I) in UIIC are not eligible to apply.

Also Read: Bank of Baroda SO Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Online for 1100 Wealth Executive, Credit Analyst Posts

UIIC AO Eligibility Criteria

Candidates applying for UIIC AO Recruitment 2026 must satisfy the Nationality/Citizenship condition as on the date of application. A candidate must be either a citizen of India, a subject of Nepal, a subject of Bhutan, a Tibetan refugee who came to India before 1st January 1962 with the intention of permanently settling in India, or a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia, or Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India. Candidates in the last four categories must hold an eligibility certificate issued by the Government of India.

UIIC AO Qualification

The minimum educational qualification must have been obtained on or before 30.06.2026 from a recognised university or institute, approved by UGC/AICTE, through the 10+2+3 pattern or an equivalent system. Working knowledge of computers is mandatory for all candidates.

Discipline Minimum Educational Qualification
Generalists Graduate or Postgraduate degree in any discipline (including Engineering, Arts, Science, Commerce, Agriculture, Data Science, etc.) from a recognised university with a minimum of 60% marks (55% for SC/ST/PwBD category)
Hindi Officers Master’s Degree from a recognised university with Hindi and English in any of the specified combinations (as compulsory/elective subject or medium of examination) at the degree level, with a minimum of 60% marks (55% for SC/ST/PwBD category)

Where only CGPA/OGPA/SGPA is awarded, candidates must produce a conversion certificate from the university; a fraction such as 59.99% will be treated as less than 60%.

UIIC AO Age Limit

As on 30.06.2026, the minimum age is 21 years and the maximum age is 30 years. Candidates must have been born not earlier than 30.06.1996 and not later than 30.06.2005 (both dates inclusive). Upper age relaxation is available as follows, subject to a cumulative cap of 45 years.

Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

UIIC AO Application Fee

The application fee/service charges are non-refundable under any circumstances, once paid.

Category of Applicant Amount (Non-Refundable)
All applicants other than SC/ST/PwBD/permanent employees of UIIC ₹1,000/- (application fee including service charges) + GST as applicable
SC/ST/PwBD/permanent employees of UIIC Application fee: Nil. ₹250/- (service charges only) + GST as applicable

Also Read: PMBI Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Offline for 178 Pharmacist, Executive and More Posts

UIIC AO Salary

Selected candidates will draw basic pay in the scale of ₹82,485-4050(14)-139185-4390(4)-156745, along with other admissible allowances. In addition to emoluments, the Company provides Gratuity, LTS, Medical Benefits, Group Personal Accident Insurance, and National Pension System (NPS), with leased accommodation extended as per Company rules. Gross pay is approximately ₹1,10,000 per month at Metropolitan centres.

Selected candidates will serve a probation period of one year (extendable at the Company’s discretion) and must pass the non-life Licentiate Examination conducted by the Insurance Institute of India during probation. Candidates must also execute a guarantee bond to serve the Company for a minimum of five years, including the probation period; early resignation attracts liquidated damages plus a ₹35,000 onboarding and integration cost.

UIIC AO Selection Process

Selection for UIIC AO Recruitment 2026 is through a three-stage process: Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, and Interview.

  • Tier I – Preliminary Examination (Qualifying, 100 marks, 60 minutes): English Language (30 questions/30 marks), Reasoning (35/35), Quantitative Aptitude (35/35).
  • Tier II – Main Examination for Generalists: Objective Test of 250 marks (English Language, Reasoning, Quantitative Aptitude, General Awareness with special reference to the Financial Sector, and Computer Knowledge – 200 questions, 150 minutes) followed by a Descriptive Test of 30 marks (Letter Writing and Essay, 30 minutes).
  • Tier II – Main Examination for Hindi Officers: Objective Test of 200 marks (English Language, Reasoning, Professional Knowledge of Hindi/English, General Awareness, Computer Knowledge – 150 questions, 120 minutes) followed by a Descriptive Test of 50 marks (English/Hindi essay, letter writing, and translation, 60 minutes).
  • Interview: Candidates qualifying the Main Examination are called for interview, up to three times the vacancies in the respective category/discipline.

For Generalists, the final merit list is prepared using Main Examination Objective Test marks and Interview marks in the ratio 75:25; Preliminary and Descriptive Test marks are not counted for merit. For Hindi Officers, the Main Examination (Objective + Descriptive) and Interview marks are considered in the ratio 75:25; Preliminary Examination marks are not counted for merit. There is a penalty of one-fourth of the marks assigned to a question for each wrong answer in the objective tests.

Documents Required

  • Scanned photograph (4.5cm x 3.5cm, colour, light background)
  • Scanned signature in black ink (not in capital letters)
  • Scanned left thumb impression on white paper with black or blue ink
  • Handwritten declaration in English, in the candidate’s own handwriting, as per the prescribed format
  • Valid Call Letter and original Photo Identity proof (PAN Card, Passport, Driving License, Voter’s Card, Bank Passbook with photograph, or similar accepted ID) at the time of examination and interview
  • Category/community, age, and educational qualification certificates, as applicable, at the time of interview

Ration cards and Learner’s Driving Licences are not accepted as valid photo ID proof.

How to Apply for UIIC AO Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the Recruitment section on the UIIC official website and click on “Apply Online”.
  2. Choose “Click here for New Registration” and enter your name, contact details, and email ID to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  3. Log in and fill in the application form, using the “Save and Next” option to complete it in stages.
  4. Upload your photograph, signature, left thumb impression, and handwritten declaration as per the specified format and size.
  5. Preview the completed application form and verify all details carefully.
  6. Click “Complete Registration” only after confirming all details are correct, as no changes are permitted afterward.
  7. Proceed to the Payment tab and pay the applicable application fee/service charges online.
  8. Click “Submit” and take a printout of the system-generated application form and payment receipt for future reference.

Important Instructions

  • Applications must be submitted online only; no other mode of application will be accepted.
  • No change of category, discipline, or application data will be permitted after registration is complete.
  • Candidates should apply well before the last date to avoid last-minute technical issues.
  • The initial posting period is a minimum of five years, and requests for transfer to a preferred location will not be entertained.
  • Candidates must keep their registered email ID and mobile number active throughout the recruitment process, as all official communication will be sent there.
  • Any dispute arising from this recruitment is subject to the sole jurisdiction of the courts in Chennai.

  • Duration: 90 minutes (120 minutes for PwBD candidates eligible for scribe assistance).

  • Minimum qualifying marks: UR/EWS 40%, OBC-NCL & SC 30%, ST 25% (relaxable by 2 marks for PwBD where vacancies remain unfilled).
